text.p: Frontier Corp., the nation's fifth-largest long distance telephone company, said Tuesday it named Joseph Clayton as president and chief operating officer, effective June 16.
He will be responsible for the day-to-day operation of the $2.5 billion telecommunications company.
Most recently, Clayton was executive vice president of marketing and sales for the Americas and Asia at Thomson Consumer Electronics.
The position of president and chief operating officer was vacated by William Oberlin 18 months ago, the company said.
A company spokesman said Clayton "would be a strong candidate" to replace Chairman and Chief Executive Ronald Bittner "if and when Mr. Bittner decides to retire."
Frontier, based in Rochester, N.Y., is a long distance, local telephone and cellular carrier.
Its stock rose 37.5 cents to $19.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
